content.thinking: Since the writer lives outside the repository, this really does depend on it changing — the old deployed revision can't be fixed since its reader logic is already baked in, so the only viable fix is at the external writer.

input.explanation: Yes. The failures happen in the old revision's reader, which is already deployed and can't be changed now. The fix only stops them if the old revision never sees '2400/8' under the bare shopper id, and that depends on how the new revision writes entries. That write isn't in this repository: only the `LookUpSummary` read seam and `SummaryEntry.__str__` (the text format) are here. Whatever puts entries into the cache, in the code that supplies the seam to `serve_account_page`, would have to write `str(entry)` under `summary_cache_key(shopper_id)` ('spend-summary:v2:{shopper_id}'), not under the bare shopper id. The fetcher it passes in would also have to accept that key. Until that writer changes, the two-field entries still land where the old revision reads, and this patch on its own would only make the new revision miss its own entries.
